newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada settles former PM Mulroney's libel suit.
newsitem.headline: Canada settles former PM Mulroney's libel suit.

text.p: Former Prime Minister Brian Mulroney has reached an out-of-court settlement in his C$50 million ($37 million) libel lawsuit against the Canadian government, his lawyers said on Monday.

Mulroney's lawyers revealed the settlement in a Montreal court where the unprecedented libel suit was to be heard. In the settlement reached on Sunday, the government apologised for wrongly accusing Mulroney of taking kickbacks in Air Canada's C$1.8 billion ($1.3 billion) purchase of Airbus jets in 1988.

Reading from the settlement in court, Mulroney's lawyer Gerald Tremblay said a letter sent by Canada's Justice Department to Swiss authorities in September 1995 wrongly indicated that Mulroney had engaged in criminal activity in the Airbus purchase.
Tremblay said the settlement specifies that the government and Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) "regret any damage to Mr. Mulroney and his family and fully apologise to them."
Tremblay said the RCMP had agreed to pay Mulroney's legal costs, while the former prime minister has agreed to waive his claim to damages in the libel action.
Outside the courtroom, Claude Armand Sheppard, a lawyer for the federal government, said he was pleased with the settlement.
